title: Deep learning predicts DNA damage response protein levels from routine slides
summary: Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning on frozen pathology foundation-model tile embeddings predicted reverse-phase protein array pathway scores from 1,673 TCGA haematoxylin-and-eosin whole-slide images covering 1,527 patients with breast, endometrial, cervical and ovarian cancer and uterine carcinosarcoma. For the 11-protein DNA damage composite the out-of-fold Spearman correlation was 0.43 against 0.31 for a cancer-type-mean baseline, about 0.29-0.30 within cancer type, and at most 0.00 with shuffled targets. Cross-validation was cancer-type-stratified and site-grouped. This is a moderate retrospective association in one public cohort: there is no external validation, no clinical or treatment-response outcome, and the authors list separating the signal from proliferation as future work, noting the cell-cycle score was predicted more strongly.
ai_technology: Gated attention-based multiple-instance learning over frozen UNI2-h and Virchow2 tile embeddings jointly regresses six RPPA pathway scores.
organization: Johns Hopkins University; Johns Hopkins School of Medicine

evidence.tested: Five-fold cancer-type-stratified, site-grouped cross-validation against measured RPPA values, compared with a cancer-type-mean baseline and a shuffled-target control.
evidence.unknown: No external cohort; no clinical or therapy-response outcome; the signal is not separated from proliferation; within-type correlation is moderate; not peer reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The attention-based model predicts DNA damage response protein scores from slide-tile embeddings.

source_review.scope: bioRxiv v1 page read: author affiliations, cohort, model, validation design, results and stated next steps; Europe PMC title search found no earlier version.
